body:
The only way to solve this (because it's a compiler ambiguity) would be to have different names for the overloads. I considered both and landed on the "same name" policy because it felt like it had better discoverability.

Honestly, this feels like something the compiler _could_ choose to fix, since it's the one that's not only matching the method but generating the signature of the lambda. So maybe someone should open that as a bug against the C# compiler. 😄

issue.title: Compiler-caused ambiguity (CS0121)

labels.name: Resolution-By Design
labels.description: The behavior reported in the issue matches the current design

repository.name: roslyn
repository.description: The Roslyn .NET compiler provides C# and Visual Basic languages with rich code analysis APIs.

issue.body:
**Version Used**: `4.7.0-3.23517.17 (9d4cc030)`

**Steps to Reproduce**:

In [xUnit.net's assertion library](https://github.com/xunit/assert.xunit) we offer overloads of functions that take either [`Task`](https://github.com/xunit/assert.xunit/blob/e48a306669184bba25bddbbacfb44113f2f3bf68/ExceptionAsserts.cs#L337) or [`ValueTask`](https://github.com/xunit/assert.xunit/blob/e48a306669184bba25bddbbacfb44113f2f3bf68/ExceptionAsserts.cs#L350). These are commonly used via lambda functions, like:

```csharp
await Assert.ThrowsAsync<DivideByZeroException>(async () => { /*...something that throws...*/ });
```

Which causes C0121:

![Screen shot from user reported issue](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1730868/279636440-4adad1a4-14fb-4b9a-b9b5-78abcafe9033.png)

The thing is...the compiler is responsible for both matching the function _and_ generating the signature of the lambda. It could easily choose either one (I assume with a preference towards `ValueTask` due to performance), but it does neither and just fails. And the syntax does not even let the user choose, so the only way around this is to write a function instead of use a lambda.

**Diagnostic Id**: `CS0121`

**Expected Behavior**:

Pick one and compile. 🎉 

**Actual Behavior**:

Make developer sad. 😢 

_Related xUnit.net issue: https://github.com/xunit/xunit/issues/2808_

body: I'm going to label this as External for the moment and see what the Roslyn team thinks.

If I end up renaming functions, I'm considering doing something that might feel a little user hostile, but for good reason, so I'm going to propose two possible solutions here to see what people think (and give people a chance to come up with another alternative.

Personally, I highly prefer Option B. I believe Option A leaves us with signatures people will likely never see, and not realize it's legal to use `ValueTask`.

### Option A

1. Remove `Assert.Throws*` overloads that take `ValueTask`
2. Add `Assert.Throws*ValueTask` overloads that take `ValueTask`

### Option B

1. Mark `Assert.Throws*` overloads as `[Obsolete]` with a message about using one of the new signatures
3. Add `Assert.Throws*Task<T>` overloads for `Task` variants
4. Add `Assert.Throws*ValueTask<T>` overloads for `ValueTask` variants

The Roslyn team just closed the issue and recommends not supporting `ValueTask` at all, so let's call that:

### Option C

1. Remove `Assert.Throws*` overloads that take `ValueTask`
2. (There is no Step 2. Just stop supporting `ValueTask`.)

issue.title: [xUnit2189] Extend xUnit1012 to test reference type nullability for InlineDataAttribute

repository.name: xunit.analyzers
repository.description: Roslyn analyzers for xUnit.net (please open issues in https://github.com/xunit/xunit)

issue.body:
Partial fix for this issue:
https://github.com/xunit/xunit/issues/2189

Extends the analyzer and fixer for xUnit1012 to checking null literals against nullability of parameter types for InlineDataAttribute. Without this change, null arguments in InlineDataAttribute are only flagged if they are to be passed to a method parameter that is value-typed and non-nullable. With this change, the analyzer also checks for nullable/non-nullable reference types, and allows the fixer to adjust it as well.

body:
I have prototyped a complete removal of `ValueTask` support (and removal of `XUNIT_VALUETASK`, which should no longer be necessary).

This includes conversions (for net-new async assertions which are currently `ValueTask` only):

- `Assert.AllAsync<T>(IEnumerable<T>, Func<T, ValueTask>)` to
   `Assert.AllAsync<T>(IEnumerable<T>, Func<T, Task>)`
- `Assert.CollectionAsync<T>(IEnumerable<T>, params Func<T, ValueTask>[])` to
   `Assert.CollectionAsync<T>(IEnumerable<T>, params Func<T, Task>[])`

And removals (for new async overloads):

- `Assert.PropertyChangedAsync(INotifyPropertyChanged, string, Func<ValueTask>)`
- `Assert.RaisesAnyAsync(Action<EventHandler>, Action<EventHandler>, Func<ValueTask>)`
- `Assert.RaisesAnyAsync<T>(Action<EventHandler<T>>, Action<EventHandler<T>>, Func<ValueTask>)`
- `Assert.RaisesAsync<T>(Action<EventHandler<T>>, Action<EventHandler<T>>, Func<ValueTask>)`
- `Assert.Throws<T>(string?, Func<ValueTask>)`
- `Assert.ThrowsAnyAsync<T>(Func<ValueTask>)`
- `Assert.ThrowsAsync(Type, Func<ValueTask>)`
- `Assert.ThrowsAsync<T>(Func<ValueTask>)`
- `Assert.ThrowsAsync<T>(string?, Func<ValueTask>)`

As expected, a few tests had to be updated to add `.AsTask()` on the end of them, because the function in question was returning `ValueTask` instead of `Task`. In my case, they were all non-async lambdas, so my choice to convert:

```csharp
await Assert.ThrowsAsync<Type>(() => ValueTaskReturningThing());
```

Included two options:

```csharp
// Use .AsTask()
await Assert.ThrowsAsync<Type>(() => ValueTaskReturningThing().AsTask());

// Use async
await Assert.ThrowsAsync<Type>(async () => await ValueTaskReturningThing());
```

I suspect a relatively low number of people were using lambdas the way that I do (my brain just won't let me force the creation of the async machinery when it's not necessary 😂).

Just updated to latest and greatest - immediately rewarded with 61 errors. Should I interpret your last comment as you will remove the overloaded support for ValueTask? If so, I will in the meantime roll-back to 2.5.3, and hopefully update to 2.6.1 soon-to-be :-)

Thanks.

For the prototype removal...

Assertion changes: https://github.com/xunit/assert.xunit/commit/5986aa7bfa07ec3ad07043e4f717ef1eb01103aa?w=1
Core framework changes: https://github.com/xunit/xunit/commit/bcff04cdb38a22db793003eafe8c19dc19b2c423?w=1

@trejjam Yeah, but:

- You still get the friction of the ambiguity error
- You have to know that syntax could fix it (since CS0121 isn't going to tell you)
- You have to be using C# 11 to fix it
